Actress Poornima Bhagyaraj is best known for essaying a number of memorable leading roles in Malayalam and Tamil cinema in the early 1980s. She started out in Bollywood, appearing supporting roles in movies like Paheli (1977) and Dillagi (1978) before landing her first big break with the Malayalam romantic thriller Manjil Virinja Pookkal (1980).
The movie, which also marked the debut of celebrated actor Mohanlal, saw Poornima playing a woman tormented by her past - a performance that won her the Kerala State Film Award for Best Actress that year.
Subsequently, Poornima established herself as one of the most sought-after leading ladies in South Indian cinema through her performances in movies like Ahimsa (1981), Payanangal Mudivathillai (1982), Mundhanai Mudichu (1983), Thanga Magan (1983) and Prasnam Gurutharam (1983).
Her performances in the Kollywood romantic drama Payanangal Mudivathillai and the Malayalam drama film Olangal (1982) won Poornima the Filmfare Award (South) for Best Actress for both the industries in the same year. Following her marriage to actor-director K. Bhagyaraj, Poornima quit acting in the mid 1980s.

About

Actress Poornima Bhagyaraj is best known for essaying a number of memorable leading roles in Malayalam and Tamil cinema in the early 1980s. She started out in Bollywood, appearing supporting roles in movies like Paheli (1977) and Dillagi (1978) before landing her first big break with the Malayalam romantic thriller Manjil Virinja Pookkal (1980). The movie, which also marked the debut of celebrated actor Mohanlal, saw Poornima playing a woman tormented by her past - a performance that won her the Kerala State Film Award for Best Actress that year. Subsequently, Poornima established herself as one of the most sought-after leading ladies in South Indian cinema through her performances in movies like Ahimsa (1981), Payanangal Mudivathillai (1982), Mundhanai Mudichu (1983), Thanga Magan (1983) and Prasnam Gurutharam (1983). Her performances in the Kollywood romantic drama Payanangal Mudivathillai and the Malayalam drama film Olangal (1982) won Poornima the Filmfare Award (South) for Best Actress for both the industries in the same year. Following her marriage to actor-director K. Bhagyaraj, Poornima quit acting in the mid 1980s. It was another 28 years before she returned to cinema with the Tamil romantic drama Aadhalal Kadhal Seiveer (2013). Among her most recent film credits are the Kollywood action drama Jilla (2014), the romantic thriller Mupparimanam (2017) and the horror thriller Mohini (2018).

Updated - April 30, 2020 02:29 pm IST

 Poornima Bhagyaraj

 Yes, I was busy with films till my marriage. Manjil Virinja Pookkal (Malayalam, 1980) was my first film. Potential women actors often choose to step away from the arc lights in favour of a quiet married life. Poornima Jayaram is one of them. A bright start and several memorable films in multiple languages later, she receded to the background after marrying leading director-actor K. Bhagyaraj. But she has kept herself busy, apart from playing the pivotal role in a close-knit family. Of late, her presence is noticed in both cinema and television. So what are her plans for the future and has the lockdown come as an unexpected roadblock? Excerpts from a chat with the actor.

Yes, I was busy with films till my marriage. *Manjil Virinja Pookkal* (Malayalam, 1980) was my first film. I went on to act in 40 Malayalam films, one each in Telugu and Bhojpuri, half-a dozen in Hindi. Majority of my films are in Tamil and Malayalam. In all about 70. Marriage changed everything and my focus was family and the outfit designing company, which I had started. I made a comeback a couple of years ago with *Aadhalal Kadhal Seiveer* . Now I’m doing both cinema and television. I made my small screen debut with ‘Kanmani’ (Sun TV). ‘Suriya Vamsam’ for Zee Tamil is another serial but now the Lockdown has interrupted shooting.

Well, I only accepted roles when I liked them. So all of them are my favourites. *Manjil Virinja Pookkal* , however, is special. For several reasons. It was the first film — not only for me but for Mohanlal, director Fazil and music director Jerry Amaldev. For actor Shankar it was his first Malayalam film.

Actress Poornima Bhagyaraj is best known for essaying a number of memorable leading roles in Malayalam and Tamil cinema in the early 1980s. She started out in Bollywood, appearing supporting roles in movies like Paheli (1977) and Dillagi (1978) before landing her first big break with the Malayalam romantic thriller Manjil Virinja Pookkal (1980). The movie, which also marked the debut of celebrated actor Mohanlal, saw Poornima playing a woman tormented by her past - a performance that won her the Kerala State Film Award for Best Actress that year.

It was another 28 years before she returned to cinema with the Tamil romantic drama Aadhalal Kadhal Seiveer (2013). ##### Biography

Actress Poornima Bhagyaraj is best known for essaying a number of memorable leading roles in Malayalam and Tamil cinema in the early 1980s. 

She started out in Bollywood, appearing in supporting roles in movies like Paheli (1977) and Dillagi (1978) before landing her first big break with the Malayalam romantic thriller Manjil Virinja Pookkal (1980). 

The movie, which also marked the debut of celebrated actor Mohanlal, saw Poornima playing a woman tormented by her past - a performance that won her the Kerala State Film Award for Best Actress that year.

Subsequently, Poornima established herself as one of the most sought-after leading ladies in South Indian cinema through her performances in movies like Ahimsa (1981), Payanangal Mudivathillai (1982), Mundhanai Mudichu (1983), Thanga Magan (1983) and Prasnam Gurutharam (1983).

 Her performances in the Kollywood romantic drama Payanangal Mudivathillai and the Malayalam drama film Olangal (1982) won Poornima the Filmfare Award (South) for Best Actress for both industries in the same year.
